landscape-sky.description: The open pixel-art sky behind the landing screen and game surfaces.

primary.description: Primary actions, selected tiles, answer choices, and the timer.

outline.description: Control outlines, headings, progress borders, links, and high-emphasis labels.

hard-shadow.description: The dark lower layer under compact controls and contained surfaces.

soft-sky.description: Quiet progress tracks and loading details.

depth-edge.description: The slim lower edge under controls and surfaces, plus progress fill.

trainer-silver.description: The automatic Trainer Card accent for Veteran rank.

components.name: Question Surface
components.description: Every question uses the same instruction, stimulus, response, and action regions within the existing panel. The instruction stays directly below the heading. Minimum region sizes keep ordinary questions aligned while allowing long content and enlarged text to grow without clipping. Text choices use four rows on mobile and two columns on desktop. Type-answer lists longer than four options use the searchable type picker. Single-answer questions choose one type immediately. Multi-select questions show removable type badges and a separate Check answers action. Submitted feedback lists correct picks, wrong picks, and missed types together. Pokémon choices share the same response height and reserve their full nameplates and revealed details, including concealed silhouettes. Short desktop screens retain the stacked structure rather than squeezing a second answer grid beside artwork.

components.description: Long type-answer lists show every available type as a pickable badge button in a responsive six, four, or three column grid. Single-answer questions choose immediately; multi-select questions toggle buttons and use Check answers. Feedback shows correct picks, wrong picks, and missed types together.
components.css: .ds-type-preview { container-type: inline-size; width: min(100%, 36rem); font-family: var(--font-interface, 'Gabarito Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-type-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 0.55rem; } .ds-type-choice { position: relative; display: grid; min-width: 0; min-height: 3.2rem; padding: 0.35rem; color: var(--primary-text, #e8fcff); background: var(--blue, #0d6be6); border: 3px solid var(--navy, #083b7e); border-radius: 0.5rem; box-shadow: inset 0 0.1rem 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12), 0 0.22rem 0 var(--yellow, #eed23e), 0 0.3rem 0 var(--navy-shadow, #123f76); cursor: pointer; place-items: center; transition: transform 100ms ease, box-shadow 100ms ease, filter 100ms ease; } .ds-type-choice:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-type-choice:active { transform: translateY(0.22rem); box-shadow: 0 0.08rem 0 var(--yellow, #eed23e), 0 0.12rem 0 var(--navy-shadow, #123f76); } .ds-type-choice:focus-visible { outline: 0.2rem solid var(--navy, #083b7e); outline-offset: 0.2rem; } .ds-type-choice[aria-pressed='true'] { color: var(--navy, #083b7e); background: var(--yellow, #eed23e); } .ds-type-choice img { width: min(100%, 3.125rem); height: auto; aspect-ratio: 5 / 2; image-rendering: pixelated; } .ds-type-choice kbd { position: absolute; top: 0.1rem; right: 0.1rem; display: grid; width: 1.1rem; height: 1.1rem; color: currentColor; background: var(--navy, #083b7e); border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 0.2rem; font-family: var(--font-data, 'Martian Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.72rem; line-height: 1; place-items: center; } @container (max-width: 35rem) { .ds-type-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr)); } } @container (max-width: 24rem) { .ds-type-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); } }

narrative.overview:
Quizmon's Logo Echo world starts with two binding identity assets: the exact Pokémon-like wordmark and the crisp pixel-art landscape. Interface chrome borrows their visual confidence without simulating a whole handheld console. Small cream and cobalt surfaces use deep navy outlines, slim yellow lower edges, compact corners, and modest hard shadows.

The landing screen centers the exact wordmark above compact Daily and Training controls. The existing landscape, fonts, palette, buttons, and Trainer artwork remain unchanged. Question, result, and setup states retain the same compact cream and navy visual language.

The result is playful, direct, and tactile. It avoids generic application chrome and keeps the quiz itself visually dominant.
keyCharacteristics: Exact wordmark and crisp landscape remain the primary identity.
Cream, cobalt, navy, and yellow controls echo the wordmark in restrained doses.
Dense game information stays clear through Gabarito and small Martian Mono numeric labels.
Hard-edged depth makes controls feel physical without adding ornamental framing.
One short transform-and-opacity entrance opens a round and its results.

rules.name: The Logo-First Rule
rules.body: Cobalt and yellow echo the wordmark. They do not compete with it by filling large decorative regions.

rules.name: The State-Color Rule
rules.body: Green and rose communicate answer or error state only. Do not use them as general accents.

rules.name: The No-Pixel-Font Rule
rules.body: Do not use bitmap or novelty pixel fonts. Pixel character comes from the landscape, not from reduced text legibility.

rules.name: The Wordmark-Is-Art Rule
rules.body: Render the approved wordmark asset. Never recreate or approximate it with live type.

rules.name: The Open-Landing Rule
rules.body: Do not place the wordmark and landing actions inside a full-page card or simulated device frame.

rules.name: The Modest-Hard-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Keep depth short, opaque, and downward. Do not replace it with diffuse elevation or a glow.

rules.name: The Compact-Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners should feel friendly but controlled. Avoid pills, circles for rectangular actions, and broad soft cards.

rules.name: The Earned-Score Rule
rules.body: Animate the points each Training answer actually earned; never present retired whole-round factors as if they contributed to the score.

dos: Do preserve the exact wordmark and crisp pixel-art landscape.
Do keep the home screen compact, button-led, and surrounded by scenery.
Do use Gabarito for interface text and reserve Martian Mono for compact data and scores.
Do preserve hard edges on pixel sprites and natural rendering on illustrated Pokémon artwork.
Do give buttons a physical pressed state through synchronized translation and compressed lower shadows.
Do animate the start and finish of a round, keep its question surface stable, and honor reduced motion.
Do prefer AVIF and WebP while retaining the provenance-bearing PNG plate fallbacks.
Do keep footer support, contact, help, and production credits readable; place full ownership and affiliation notices on the Terms page.
donts: Don't build a giant HUD, simulated handheld frame, or full-page landing card.
Don't use glass panels, blurred scenery, gradients, or diffuse floating-card shadows.
Don't introduce pixel-font overkill, oversized uppercase labels, or decorative game glyphs.
Don't force Pokémon sprites onto type, move, or ability choices that do not represent Pokémon.
Don't add navigation, marketing copy, characters, ornamental frames, or ball symbols beyond functional game progression to fill open space.
Don't redesign, redraw, crop, blur, or place the wordmark inside another container.
Don't let decoration obscure answers, progress, score, modifiers, or keyboard focus.
